concepts.name: Mechanisms of Sea Level Rise: Thermal Expansion vs. Ice Melt Contribution
key_dimensions: Relative contribution of thermal expansion (~40-50%) vs. glacial/ice sheet melt (~50-60%) to observed rise
Steric sea level rise (density-driven) vs. eustatic sea level rise (mass addition) — definitional traps
Why thermal expansion dominates in short term but ice melt dominates in long-term projections
UPSC trap: distinguishing between sea ice melt (no contribution) vs. land ice melt (contributes to rise)

concepts.name: Greenland Ice Sheet vs. Antarctic Ice Sheet: Differential Risk Profiles
key_dimensions: Greenland melt potential (~7m rise) vs. West Antarctic Ice Sheet (~3.3m) vs. East Antarctic (~53m) — comparative magnitudes
Marine Ice Sheet Instability (MISI) and Marine Ice Cliff Instability (MICI) — tipping point mechanisms
Albedo feedback loop specific to each ice sheet and its acceleration potential
UPSC trap: East Antarctica is largely stable currently but holds highest potential; West Antarctica is the active risk

concepts.name: Observed vs. Projected Sea Level Rise: IPCC AR6 Benchmarks
key_dimensions: Historical rate: ~1.4 mm/year (1901–1990) vs. ~3.7 mm/year (2006–2018) — acceleration trend
IPCC AR6 projections: likely range under SSP1-2.6 (~0.3–0.6m) vs. SSP5-8.5 (~0.6–1.0m) by 2100
Low-likelihood, high-impact scenario of >2m rise if ice sheet instabilities triggered
UPSC trap: difference between 'committed' sea level rise (already locked in) and 'projected' rise under scenarios

concepts.name: Relative Sea Level Rise vs. Absolute Sea Level Rise
key_dimensions: Absolute (eustatic) rise measured by satellite altimetry vs. relative rise incorporating land subsidence
Role of land subsidence due to groundwater extraction, sediment compaction (e.g., Mumbai, Chennai, Jakarta)
Post-glacial rebound (isostatic uplift) in Scandinavia causing apparent sea level fall despite global rise
UPSC trap: cities can face greater flooding risk than global average due to subsidence even if absolute rise is moderate

concepts.name: Regional Variability in Sea Level Rise: Unequal Distribution
key_dimensions: Gravitational fingerprinting: melting Greenland ice reduces gravity pull, causing sea level rise AWAY from Greenland (counterintuitive UPSC trap)
Ocean circulation changes (AMOC weakening) causing higher rise along US East Coast
Indian Ocean and Bay of Bengal showing above-average rise rates affecting South Asian coastlines
Role of ENSO and IOD in interannual variability of regional sea levels

concepts.name: Impacts on Small Island Developing States (SIDS) and Atoll Nations
key_dimensions: Existential threat to Maldives, Tuvalu, Kiribati, Marshall Islands — potential complete submergence
Tuvalu's treaty with Australia (2023 Falepili Union) — 'world's first climate mobility treaty' — novel legal precedent
Loss of EEZ (Exclusive Economic Zone) if land territory submerges — UNCLOS ambiguity and ongoing negotiations
UPSC trap: distinction between habitability loss (salinization, storm surge) which occurs BEFORE physical submergence

concepts.name: Sea Level Rise and Indian Coastline: Vulnerability Assessment
key_dimensions: India's 7,516 km coastline; Sundarbans losing ~7,500 hectares between 1970-2018
Sagar Island and Ghoramara Island (West Bengal) as active submergence case studies
INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services) role in monitoring and early warning
Differential vulnerability: flat deltaic coasts (Bengal, Odisha) vs. rocky coasts (Kerala, Goa) — UPSC comparison trap

concepts.name: Sundarbans: Sea Level Rise, Mangrove Loss, and Ecosystem Cascade
key_dimensions: Rate of sea level rise in Sundarbans (~3–8mm/year) vs. global average — above average due to subsidence
Mangroves as natural buffers: how their loss creates positive feedback accelerating coastal erosion
Ecological-social nexus: Bengal tiger habitat loss, fisherfolk displacement, salinity intrusion in agriculture
UNESCO World Heritage Site status vs. development pressures — governance conflict angle

concepts.name: Coastal Flooding, Storm Surge Amplification, and Compound Events
key_dimensions: Mechanism: baseline sea level rise converts '1-in-100-year' floods to '1-in-10-year' events
Compound events: simultaneous sea level rise + storm surge + heavy rainfall (e.g., Chennai floods 2015 analysis)
Cyclone intensity and storm surge relationship in Bay of Bengal — above-average vulnerability
UPSC trap: sea level rise alone doesn't cause flooding — it's the interaction with tides and weather that creates 'nuisance flooding'

concepts.name: Saltwater Intrusion: Freshwater Security and Agricultural Impacts
key_dimensions: Mechanism of saltwater intrusion into coastal aquifers and river deltas
Impact on Ganges-Brahmaputra delta agriculture: rice cultivation shift, loss of agricultural land
Drinking water crisis in coastal cities — Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai aquifer salinization
UPSC trap: saltwater intrusion impacts occur well before physical land submergence — it's a precursor threat

concepts.name: Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) and Sea Level Rise Linkage
key_dimensions: AMOC slowdown caused by freshwater influx from Greenland melt disrupting thermohaline circulation
Paradox: AMOC weakening causes regional sea level rise along US East Coast and Northwestern Europe despite global pattern
AMOC as a tipping element — potential abrupt collapse scenario and its cascading global climate effects
UPSC trap: AMOC slowdown is both a consequence AND an amplifier of climate change — bidirectional relationship

concepts.name: Climate Migration and Sea Level Rise: Legal and Governance Gaps
key_dimensions: 1951 Refugee Convention does not recognize 'climate refugees' — critical legal gap
Distinction between climate migrants, climate refugees, and internally displaced persons (IDP) in international law
Nansen Initiative and Platform on Disaster Displacement — non-binding frameworks for climate mobility
UPSC trap: 'climate refugee' has NO legal definition under international law — people displaced by sea level rise have no protected status

concepts.name: Managed Retreat as Coastal Adaptation Strategy: Policy and Ethics
key_dimensions: Definition: planned relocation of communities and infrastructure away from high-risk coastal zones
CRZ (Coastal Regulation Zone) Notification 2019 in India — relaxations that increase vulnerability vs. original 1991 intent
Ethical dimensions: displacement of indigenous/fishing communities vs. long-term safety — environmental justice angle
UPSC trap: CRZ 2019 relaxed restrictions in some areas (allowing construction closer to coast) — opposite direction to adaptation logic

concepts.name: Hard vs. Soft Coastal Engineering Adaptation Measures
key_dimensions: Hard infrastructure: seawalls, storm surge barriers (Thames Barrier, Rotterdam approach), their limitations and terminal costs
Soft measures: beach nourishment, mangrove restoration, coral reef protection as living shorelines
Nature-based Solutions (NbS) vs. grey infrastructure — cost-benefit comparison and co-benefits
UPSC trap: hard infrastructure can cause 'coastal squeeze' — eliminating intertidal habitat between seawall and rising sea

concepts.name: Loss and Damage Framework: Sea Level Rise as the Central Case
key_dimensions: COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh, 2022) establishment of Loss and Damage Fund — breakthrough after 30 years of negotiation
COP28 (Dubai, 2023): operationalization of the fund, hosted by World Bank (contested by developing nations)
Distinction: Loss and Damage vs. Adaptation (unavoidable impacts) vs. Mitigation (preventing impacts)
UPSC trap: Loss and Damage deliberately avoids the word 'compensation' to prevent legal liability for developed nations — political compromise

concepts.name: Tipping Points and Non-Linear Sea Level Rise: Beyond IPCC Likely Range
key_dimensions: Definition of tipping points: thresholds beyond which change becomes self-sustaining (e.g., ice-albedo feedback, permafrost methane)
Interaction between tipping elements: Greenland melt → AMOC slowdown → Amazon dieback cascade
Significance of 1.5°C vs. 2°C threshold for likelihood of crossing major ice sheet tipping points
UPSC trap: IPCC 'likely range' explicitly excludes low-probability high-impact scenarios — the 2m+ scenario is real but unquantified

concepts.name: Measuring Sea Level Rise: Tide Gauges vs. Satellite Altimetry
key_dimensions: Tide gauges measure relative sea level (local); satellite altimetry (TOPEX/Poseidon, Jason series, Sentinel-6) measures absolute rise
GRACE and GRACE-FO satellites measure ice mass loss through gravity changes — indirect measurement method
Discrepancies between methods and how they are reconciled in IPCC assessments
UPSC trap: tide gauge data shows more variability due to land movement; satellite data gives cleaner global signal — each has specific utility

concepts.name: Coral Bleaching, Reef Degradation, and Coastal Protection Loss
key_dimensions: Coral reefs as natural breakwaters reducing wave energy by ~97% — quantified ecosystem service
Dual threat: ocean warming (bleaching) + ocean acidification (dissolution) undermining reef structure
Sea level rise pace vs. coral growth rate: reefs can 'keep up' with slow rise but not accelerated rise
UPSC trap: even dead coral skeletons provide some protection, but ocean acidification dissolves carbonate skeletons — complete structural loss possible

concepts.name: Urban Coastal Infrastructure Risk: Financial and Planning Dimensions
key_dimensions: Global exposure: ~1 billion people live within 10m elevation of sea level; $1 trillion+ in coastal infrastructure at risk
Mumbai's vulnerability: Bandra-Kurla Complex, airports, and low-lying slums (Dharavi) below 5m elevation
Concept of 'stranded assets': long-lived coastal infrastructure becoming unusable before design life ends
UPSC trap: insurance withdrawal from high-risk coastal zones is already occurring — creating 'uninsurability' crisis before physical impacts peak
